wal: plan an explanation text by choosing skills and organising information in a boxing-up grid
tib: This is so my draft is focused and well-structured before I start writing.
isb: completing a boxing-up grid with a chosen introduction, three or four skill sections and a conclusion.

title: Grammar Warm-Up
subtitle: Odd one out. Which item in each group does NOT belong in an explanation text?

cards.label: Group 1
lines: A)  A rhetorical question
B)  A subheading
C)  A time connective:
‘The next morning…’
Which is the odd one out?

cards.label: Group 2
lines: A)  Present tense verbs
B)  Third person writing
C)  A character’s feelings:
‘He felt afraid.’
Which is the odd one out?

cards.label: Group 3
lines: A)  ‘As a result,’
B)  ‘Therefore,’
C)  ‘Suddenly,’
Which is the odd one out?

title: Choosing your three or four skills.
lines: You are writing for a house cat who has never left home.
They are stepping into the city for the first time.
Think carefully:
•  Which skills keep a cat safe from the very start?
•  Which skills would be hardest to learn without guidance?
•  Which skills have the most interesting HOW and WHY to explain?
Talk to your partner. Choose three or four skills.
Be ready to explain WHY you chose those particular ones.

title: Building the boxing-up grid.
left_label: What I need in each box
right_lines: What it is: being ready to
How it works: look at problems

title: Planning together.
lines: Let’s plan the Awareness section as a class.
Subheading: Awareness
What is the skill?
The city is full of sights, sounds and smells.
A cat must pay attention to everything around it.
How does it work?
Listen carefully, watch closely, trust your senses.
What happens as a result?
Spot trouble before it reaches you.
Now: how would you write the ‘how it works’ sentence using a connective?

title: Complete your boxing-up grid.
lines: Fill in your boxing-up grid independently.
For each chosen skill, complete all four rows:
•  Subheading
•  What the skill is
•  How it works
•  What happens as a result
Do not write full sentences yet.
Notes and key words are enough.
When you have finished, discuss your plan with a partner.
Check: does each section explain both HOW and WHY?

q1: Was it hard to choose which skills to include? What helped you decide?
q2: Why is it important to include both HOW and WHY in each section, not just WHAT the skill is?
q3: Looking at your plan, which section do you think will be the strongest in your draft?
